55: ## 3. 架构和资源所有权
56: 
57: ### 3.1 固定架构结论
58: 
59: - BK7258 AP 是 Cortex-M33 / ARMv8-M Mainline / Thumb / hard-float，不是 Cortex-A / ARMv8-A。
60: - 不得引入 `arch/arm64`、GIC、AArch64、generic timer、MMU/页表、TF-A/BL31 或 `OUTPUT_ARCH(aarch64)`。
61: - BK7258 是三核 AMP：物理 CPU0 运行 Armino CP，CPU1 是 OpenVela AP primary，CPU2 是 AP secondary。
62: - AP 内部 SMP 时 CPU1/CPU2 运行同一个 `nuttx.bin`，映射为 NuttX 逻辑 CPU0/CPU1。
63: - 当前运行基线是 CPU1 单核，CPU2 SMP 尚未实现。
64: 
65: ### 3.2 CPU0/CP 保留职责
66: 
67: CP 继续拥有并负责：
68: 
69: - bootloader、CP 固件和 FreeRTOS 运行环境
70: - 中央电源/时钟管理、硬件 WDT
71: - PSRAM PHY、电压、时钟、控制器和器件 ID 检测
72: - Flash 擦写编程
73: - Wi-Fi controller、RWNX/UMAC/LMAC/MAC/PHY/RF
74: - Bluetooth BTDM controller-only
75: - CP UART0 物理日志口
76: 
77: AP 不得重复执行与 CP 冲突的 PHY、时钟、电源或控制器初始化。
78: 
79: ### 3.3 内存地址来源
80: 
81: Flash、SRAM、PSRAM 和保留区地址来自目标 `app_ab` 分区生成结果，不是 BK7258 芯片常量：
82: 
83: ```text
84: AP Flash XIP:    0x02150000 (当前 app_ab 布局)
85: AP 私有 SRAM:    0x28010000..0x28064000 (336 KiB)
86: AP_SPINLOCK:     0x28000000..0x2800ffff
87: CP_RAM:          0x28064000..0x2809f6ff
88: PWR_MNG:         0x2809f700..0x2809f7ff
89: PSRAM 窗口:      0x60000000..0x60ffffff (当前 16 MiB 布局)
90: ```
91: 
92: AP 不得清零 CP_RAM、PWR_MNG、SWAP，不得把 `AP_SPINLOCK` 放入 heap，不得覆盖 CP 的 128 KiB PSRAM heap。
93: 
94: ### 3.4 AP 镜像注入
95: 
96: AP 镜像只能通过 `EXTERNAL_AP_BIN` 接口注入打包流程，不得手工覆盖 `package/tmp/app1.bin`。
97: 
98: ### 3.5 AP 控制台
99: 
100: 正式 AP 日志路径是 Mailbox UART -> CP UART0。物理 UART1 不是交付控制台，不接管 GPIO0/1。
101: 
102: ### 3.6 安全状态
103: 
104: 当前 Secure alias / CMSE 只表示按现有 AP 的 SPE 编译属性建立功能基线，不等于镜像已通过 secure boot。在安全启动、OTP/eFuse 和 CPU1 镜像认证闭环前，输出只能标注为开发构建。

1: # VelaSight 双场景应用功能规划
2: 
3: ## 1. 功能目标与场景
4: 
5: VelaSight 在用户按键授权后，以固定 5 FPS 采集人脸 JPEG，并连续采集
6: 16 kHz、16 bit、单声道音频。云端实时完成表情识别和语音转写，维护本次
7: 会话的结构化文字时间线；用户按下结束键后，云端将完整时间线交给大模型，
8: 生成总结、沟通建议、情绪比例和完整记录并返回设备。逻辑上，设备只与一个
9: 统一 AI 接口交互；云端内部负责接收媒体、调用必要的小模型/ASR、组织大模型
10: 请求和转发结果，不向设备暴露多个模型服务。完整结果返回设备后由设备本地存储，云端删除本次会话
11: 的临时数据。这是“社交辅助模式”。
12: 
13: 设备闲置时提供“闲时语音助手模式”。用户按键发起一次语音交互，设备端
14: `ai_agent` 将用户请求与获准使用的本地内容拼接为 Prompt，直接调用大模型
15: 服务，不经过自建会话云。模型返回回答文本和 TTS 音频，设备以扬声器播报，
16: 屏幕只显示简短状态和摘要。若所选模型接口不直接接收音频，设备调用同一
17: 模型服务商的 ASR 接口先取得文本，仍不经过自建会话云。
18: 
19: 系统只提供沟通线索，不进行人脸身份识别、人格判断、心理或医学诊断。
20: 所有结论使用“可能”等非确定性表述，线索不足时返回“无法判断”。
21: 
22: ### 1.1 社交辅助模式
23: 
24: - 用户明确开始和结束一次社交记录。
25: - 固定 5 FPS 图像采样与连续音频采集同时运行。
26: - 设备将图像和音频发送到统一的云端 AI 接口；云端内部完成表情识别、ASR 和
27:   大模型编排，设备不感知内部模型拆分。
28: - 记录期间可返回显著情绪即时提示；结束后返回带标题和正文的完整记录。
29: - 主要输出为屏幕摘要、震动提示和用户确认后的 TTS 播报。
30: 
31: ### 1.2 闲时语音助手模式
32: 
33: - 用户按键唤起一次交互，不使用常开麦克风和语音唤醒。
34: - Camera 默认关闭，不进行表情识别，不创建云端社交会话。
35: - `ai_agent` 在设备本地读取白名单内容，构造 Prompt 后直接请求大模型。
36: - 本地内容可包括设备状态、用户选择的历史结果摘要和配置，不默认附加原始
37:   音频、人脸图片、API Key、系统日志或未授权的完整历史记录。
38: - 大模型回答以 TTS 为主要输出；屏幕仅显示“聆听、思考、播报、失败”等状态
39:   以及一至两行摘要，避免受限屏幕承担长文本阅读。
40: - 用户可在本地历史记录列表中选择一条社交记录，交给 `ai_agent` 发起闲时
41:   回顾交互；回顾请求只提交选中的记录和用户问题，不上传其他历史记录。
42: - 一轮问答结束后回到闲时待机；不在设备端维护无限增长的多轮上下文。
43: 
44: ## 2. 三层架构
45: 
46: ### 2.1 设备感知与交互层（BK7258/OpenVela）
47: 
48: 负责两种模式的选择、采集、传输、本地 Agent 编排和结果呈现，不在 MCU 上
49: 执行复杂模型推理。
50: 
51: - 三键交互：模式/下一项、开始/结束/确认、取消/静音。
52: - 开始前显示采集和隐私提示，用户确认后创建会话。
53: - Camera 固定采样 5 FPS，采用 480x480 或 640x480 硬件 JPEG。
54: - Audio 连续采集 16 kHz、16 bit、单声道音频，并按固定时长分块上传。
55: - 为图片和音频附加 `session_id`、序号和单调时钟时间戳。
56: - 使用有界缓冲和丢旧帧策略；网络拥塞不能阻塞音频、Mailbox heartbeat
57:   或按键响应。
58: - 屏幕不显示实时预览，仅在按键、状态和结果变化时响应式刷新。
59: - 社交模式用震动提示开始、结果到达和失败；详细 TTS 默认由用户确认后播放。
60: - 收到最终结果后保存或展示结构化记录，并向云端发送接收确认。
61: - 取消、超时或异常时停止采集，释放 PSRAM 中的原始图片和音频。
62: - 闲时模式由 `ai_agent` 读取白名单本地内容、构造 Prompt 并直接调用模型 API。
63: - 闲时模式按键开始录音、按键结束录音；取得回答后下载 TTS 二进制并播放。
64: - TTS 播放支持按键打断；打断后停止 DAC、释放音频缓冲并返回待机。
65: 
66: ### 2.2 云端会话与模型编排层
67: 
68: 只服务社交辅助模式，负责设备接入、媒体预处理、内部模型调用、统一请求
69: 路由和临时数据清理。该层对设备表现为一个统一的大模型接口；闲时语音助手
70: 和本地历史回顾不经过该社交会话层。
71: 
72: - 鉴权并创建唯一 `session_id`，拒绝超长、越序或不属于当前会话的数据。
73: - 每张 JPEG 到达后执行图像质量、人脸存在性和表情小模型识别。
74: - 音频块到达后执行增量 ASR，生成带起止时间的语音字幕。
75: - 将表情类别、置信度和 ASR 字幕按时间合并为会话时间线。
76: - 活跃会话只暂存完成推理所需的数据；普通原始帧在小模型处理后立即删除。
77: - 低置信度且图像质量合格时，可临时保留最多 1 至 3 张关键帧交给多模态
78:   模型复核；模糊、遮挡、无人脸等无效帧直接删除。
79: - 同一显著情绪在多帧中持续且置信度达到阈值时，可调用大模型生成即时
80:   建议；该建议写入时间线，但不结束当前会话，并设置冷却时间避免重复提示。
81: - 收到结束请求后冻结时间线，计算情绪时长/帧数比例，构造一次完整请求。
82: - 校验大模型返回的 JSON Schema、枚举、长度和置信度，再路由给设备。
83: - 设备确认完整接收后删除云端的原始音频、图片、关键帧和模型中间结果；设备
84:   本地历史记录不受影响。
85: - 设备未确认时只做有限次数重传，并设置会话 TTL；TTL 到期后强制删除云端
86:   临时数据，设备可通过记录状态发起重新获取或将本次记录标记为不完整。
87: 
88: ### 2.3 模型服务与生成层
89: 
90: 包含表情小模型、ASR、大模型和 TTS。社交模式由云端会话层编排，闲时模式
91: 由设备端 `ai_agent` 直接调用允许的模型接口。
92: 
93: - 常规实时路径：表情小模型输出类别、置信度和质量原因，ASR 输出字幕。
94: - 低置信度复核路径：多模态模型结合关键帧、候选表情和对应字幕判断；仍不
95:   确定时返回“无法判断”。
96: - 显著线索路径：结合最近数秒的表情时序和字幕生成简短即时建议。
97: - 会话结束路径：基于完整时间线生成总结、建议、情绪比例和完整记录。
98: - 闲时助手路径：理解用户问题和设备提交的本地上下文，返回回答文本与 TTS
99:   音频；不能反向读取设备文件或主动调用未授权 Tool。
100: - 大模型只返回结构化内容，不返回可由设备直接执行的 Shell、寄存器或任意
101:   Tool 指令。
102: 
103: ## 3. 单向数据流
104: 
105: 每条链路只描述一个方向的数据移动。请求和响应分为不同链路，避免把设备、
106: 自建云端和模型服务之间的往返交互画成循环依赖。
107: 
108: ### 3.1 社交模式：会话建立
109: 
110: ```text
111: 建立请求：用户确认 -> 设备会话状态机 -> TLS -> 自建云端会话接口
112: 建立响应：自建云端生成 session_id -> TLS -> 设备会话状态机 -> 屏幕显示记录中
113: ```
114: 
115: ### 3.2 社交模式：图像识别流
116: 
117: ```text
118: GC2145 Camera
119:   -> 5 FPS 硬件 JPEG
120:   -> PSRAM 有界帧队列
121:   -> TLS 上传
122:   -> 自建云端图像质量检测
123:   -> 表情小模型
124:   -> 带时间戳的表情类别、置信度和无效原因
125:   -> 云端会话时间线
126: ```
127: 
128: ### 3.3 社交模式：语音字幕流
129: 
130: ```text
131: 设备侧单向上传：
132: 麦克风
133:   -> Audio ADC 16 kHz/16 bit/mono
134:   -> 有界音频分块
135:   -> 统一 AI 接口
136: 
137: 云端内部处理：
138: 音频分块 -> ASR -> 带起止时间的字幕 -> 会话上下文
139: 
140: 设备侧单向接收：
141: 会话上下文 -> 大模型请求 -> 完整文字/表情/字幕记录 -> 设备本地存储
142: ```
143: 
144: ### 3.4 社交模式：记录期即时提示流
145: 
146: ```text
147: 分析请求：持续显著线索 -> 最近数秒表情证据和字幕 -> 统一 AI 接口
148: 云端内部：统一 AI 接口 -> 必要的小模型/ASR -> 大模型即时建议
149: 模型响应：大模型结构化短建议 -> 云端 Schema 校验 -> 设备
150: 设备反馈：设备结果解析 -> 震动和屏幕短提示
151: 语音反馈：用户确认 -> 设备 TTS 播放队列 -> Audio DAC -> 扬声器
152: ```
153: 
154: ### 3.5 社交模式：低置信度复核流
155: 
156: ```text
157: 复核请求：质量合格的低置信度结果 -> 统一 AI 接口 -> 最多 1 至 3 张关键帧
158: 复核响应：多模态大模型 -> 复核结果或“无法判断” -> 统一 AI 接口 -> 设备
159: ```
160: 
161: ### 3.6 社交模式：结束与完整结果流
162: 
163: ```text
164: 结束请求：用户按结束 -> 设备停止 Camera/Audio -> 剩余音频块和结束请求
165:   -> 统一 AI 接口
166: 云端内部：字幕、表情时间线和预制 Prompt -> 大模型完整分析
167: 模型响应：大模型 -> 标题、正文、总结、建议、情绪比例和完整记录
168:   -> 统一 AI 接口 -> 设备
169: 设备处理：设备校验并保存本地历史记录 -> 屏幕显示标题和摘要 -> 可选 TTS
170: 云端清理：设备确认完整接收 -> 云端删除原始媒体和临时中间数据
171: ```
172: 
173: ### 3.7 闲时助手：请求流
174: 
175: ```text
176: 采集：用户按键 -> 麦克风短音频 -> 设备端 ai_agent 音频缓冲
177: 转写请求：ai_agent 音频缓冲 -> TLS -> 模型原生音频接口或服务商 ASR
178: 转写响应：模型服务 -> ASR 文本 -> TLS -> 设备端 ai_agent
179: 问答请求：ASR 文本 + 系统 Prompt + 用户选中的本地历史记录 -> ai_agent
180:   -> 大模型接口
181: ```
182: 
183: ### 3.8 闲时助手：回答与语音流
184: 
185: ```text
186: 问答响应：大模型回答文本 -> TLS -> 设备端 ai_agent
187: 语音请求：回答文本 -> ai_agent -> TTS 服务
188: 语音响应：TTS 二进制音频 -> TLS -> 设备有界播放缓冲 -> Audio DAC -> 扬声器
189: ```
190: 
191: ```text
192: 显示：大模型回答文本 -> 设备结果解析 -> 一至两行摘要 -> GC9D01 屏幕事件刷新
193: ```
194: 
195: ## 4. 模式与状态
196: 
197: ### 4.1 顶层模式
198: 
199: ```text
200: IDLE <-> SOCIAL_ASSIST
201: IDLE <-> VOICE_ASSIST
202: ```
203: 
204: - 两种模式互斥，不能同时占用麦克风、网络请求上下文或 TTS 播放设备。
205: - 社交记录期间不能启动闲时助手；闲时助手结束或取消后才能开始社交记录。
206: - 模式切换先停止当前 Camera/Audio/DAC，再释放缓冲和网络请求，最后刷新屏幕。
207: 
208: ### 4.2 社交模式状态
209: 
210: ```text
211: IDLE -> CONSENT -> RECORDING -> FINALIZING -> RESULT_READY -> IDLE
212:                      |              |
213:                      +-> CANCELLED <-+
214:                      +-> ERROR ------+
215: ```
216: 
217: - `RECORDING`：固定 5 FPS 图像采样和连续音频上传，云端维护实时文字时间线。
218: - `FINALIZING`：设备停止采集，云端排空在途任务并生成最终结果，禁止新媒体写入。
219: - `RESULT_READY`：设备接收标题、正文、完整文字/表情/字幕记录并写入本地；
220:   设备确认后云端清理临时数据。
221: - `CANCELLED`：立即停止推理和上传，删除本次会话数据，不生成总结。
222: - `ERROR`：向设备返回明确错误码并清理数据，不使用伪造或缓存结果替代。
223: 
224: ### 4.3 闲时助手状态
225: 
226: ```text
227: IDLE -> LISTENING -> TRANSCRIBING -> THINKING -> SPEAKING -> IDLE
228:           |              |             |           |
229:           +--------------+-> CANCELLED <-+---------+
230: ```
231: 
232: - `LISTENING`：麦克风采集短音频，Camera 和 DAC 关闭。
233: - `TRANSCRIBING`：取得用户文本；屏幕显示处理中，不显示完整字幕。
234: - `THINKING`：`ai_agent` 构造 Prompt 并等待模型回答。
235: - `SPEAKING`：屏幕显示短摘要，DAC 播放 TTS；用户可随时按键打断。
236: - `CANCELLED`：取消在途请求，停止 ADC/DAC，释放内容副本和音频缓冲。
237: 
238: ## 5. 核心数据约定
239: 
240: 所有消息必须包含 `schema_version`、`sequence` 和时间戳。社交模式使用
241: `session_id` 关联整次会话；闲时助手使用 `request_id` 关联单轮请求；本地历史
242: 记录使用 `record_id` 关联标题、正文和完整原始分析记录。
243: 
244: 云端维护的时间线条目至少包含：
245: 
246: ```json
247: {
248:   "start_ms": 5000,
249:   "end_ms": 6200,
250:   "transcript": "我不太明白刚才这一点。",
251:   "emotion": "possible_confusion",
252:   "confidence": 0.78,
253:   "evidence": "multiple_consistent_frames",
254:   "uncertainty": null
255: }
256: ```
257: 
258: 社交模式最终响应至少包含以下字段。该响应由统一 AI 接口一次性返回，设备
259: 不需要分别接收表情模型、ASR 和大模型的结果：
260: 
261: ```json
262: {
263:   "schema_version": "social-cue/v1",
264:   "session_id": "example-session-id",
265:   "status": "completed",
266:   "created_at": "2026-08-17T10:30:00Z",
267:   "title": "关于方案确认的沟通记录",
268:   "body": "本次交流主要围绕方案确认。对方在中段出现可能的困惑线索。",
269:   "summary": "交流主要围绕方案确认，对方在中段出现可能的困惑线索。",
270:   "suggestions": [
271:     "可以简要重述关键点，并确认对方是否理解。"
272:   ],
273:   "emotion_distribution": [
274:     {"emotion": "neutral", "ratio": 0.72},
275:     {"emotion": "possible_confusion", "ratio": 0.28}
276:   ],
277:   "invalid_frame_ratio": 0.08,
278:   "timeline": [
279:     {
280:       "start_ms": 5000,
281:       "end_ms": 6200,
282:       "transcript": "我不太明白刚才这一点。",
283:       "emotion": "possible_confusion",
284:       "confidence": 0.78,
285:       "evidence": "multiple_consistent_frames",
286:       "uncertainty": null
287:     }
288:   ],
289:   "full_transcript": "完整语音字幕文本",
290:   "uncertainty": "表情结果仅为辅助线索"
291: }
292: ```
293: 
294: 情绪比例必须基于有效人脸帧或有效时间窗口计算，无人脸、模糊和无法判断帧
295: 不应被归入中性表情；各有效类别比例之和为 1，`invalid_frame_ratio` 单独表示
296: 无效数据占比。
297: 
298: 闲时助手响应至少包含：
299: 
300: ```json
301: {
302:   "schema_version": "voice-assistant/v1",
303:   "request_id": "example-request-id",
304:   "sequence": 1,
305:   "timestamp_ms": 1320,
306:   "status": "completed",
307:   "answer": "完整回答文本",
308:   "display_text": "适合屏幕显示的一至两行摘要",
309:   "tts_format": "audio/ogg",
310:   "tts_length": 12345
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: 设备收到并校验最终响应后生成本地 `record_id`。历史列表至少显示
315: `record_id`、标题、时间和一行摘要。用户使用按键选择记录后，按确认键发起
316: 回顾交互；设备只把该记录的 `title`、`body`、完整文字/表情/字幕记录以及
317: 当前问题交给 `ai_agent`。历史记录内容可按长度截断，但必须明确标记截断
318: 状态，不能伪装为完整上下文。
319: 
320: 为保持设备实现最简，本地不拆分多张业务表。每次社交会话只保存一份不可变
321: 完整 JSON 记录，并额外保存一条用于屏幕列表查询的轻量索引。完整记录结构为：
322: 
323: ```json
324: {
325:   "record_id": "record-20260817-001",
326:   "created_at": "2026-08-17T10:30:00Z",
327:   "status": "complete",
328:   "title": "关于方案确认的沟通记录",
329:   "body": "本次交流主要围绕方案确认。对方在中段出现可能的困惑线索。",
330:   "summary": "对方可能在中段出现困惑，建议确认理解情况。",
331:   "emotion_distribution": [],
332:   "full_transcript": "完整语音字幕文本",
333:   "timeline": [],
334:   "suggestions": [],
335:   "source_session_id": "example-session-id",
336:   "content_truncated": false
337: }
338: ```
339: 
340: - `title` 用于历史列表和闲时回顾选择，长度应适合屏幕显示。
341: - `body` 是类似 LLM 标题+正文的可读记录，适合屏幕摘要和 TTS 播报。
342: - `full_transcript` 保存完整语音字幕；`timeline` 保存每个时间段的表情、
343:   置信度、证据和字幕，二者不能互相替代。
344: - `status=complete` 只能在标题、正文、完整字幕和完整表情记录均写入成功后
345:   设置；写入中断时保留 `incomplete`，不得出现在默认的可回顾列表中。
346: - `source_session_id` 仅用于设备本地关联和排障，不作为闲时模型的用户可见
347:   内容；云端清理会话不会删除该本地字段。
348: 
349: 轻量索引只保存列表需要的字段和完整记录位置：
350: 
351: ```json
352: {
353:   "record_id": "record-20260817-001",
354:   "created_at": "2026-08-17T10:30:00Z",
355:   "title": "关于方案确认的沟通记录",
356:   "summary": "对方可能在中段出现困惑。",
357:   "status": "complete",
358:   "record_key": "records/record-20260817-001"
359: }
360: ```
361: 
362: 按键浏览只读取轻量索引；用户确认某条记录后再按 `record_key` 读取完整 JSON，
363: 避免在受限内存中一次加载全部历史。写入顺序固定为“完整 JSON -> 校验成功
364: -> 轻量索引”，防止列表出现指向不完整数据的记录。
365: 
366: 闲时回顾请求至少包含：
367: 
368: ```json
369: {
370:   "schema_version": "voice-review/v1",
371:   "request_id": "review-request-001",
372:   "record_id": "record-20260817-001",
373:   "question": "刚才交流中对方为什么可能感到困惑？",
374:   "record": {
375:     "title": "关于方案确认的沟通记录",
376:     "body": "本次交流主要围绕方案确认。",
377:     "summary": "对方可能在中段出现困惑。",
378:     "full_transcript": "完整语音字幕文本",
379:     "timeline": [],
380:     "emotion_distribution": [],
381:     "content_truncated": false
382:   },
383:   "sequence": 1,
384:   "timestamp_ms": 123456
385: }
386: ```
387: 
388: 设备端 `ai_agent` 只从当前选中的 `record_id` 构造该请求，并限制正文、字幕、
389: 时间线和问题的总长度；超过限制时优先保留标题、正文、摘要和与问题相关的
390: 时间线片段，同时将 `content_truncated` 置为 `true`。
391: 
392: 设备必须按响应长度处理 TTS 二进制，不能使用 C 字符串结束符判断音频长度。
393: 模型服务如返回 `tts_url`，设备只允许下载 HTTPS 白名单域名且必须校验证书。
394: 
395: ## 6. 资源与隐私边界
396: 
397: - Camera 固定 5 FPS，但只保留有界数量的在途帧；队列满时丢弃最旧未处理帧。
398: - 音频优先级高于图片，任何图像任务不得造成 Audio underrun。
399: - 屏幕仅事件触发刷新，不运行实时 Camera Preview。
400: - ADC 录音与 DAC/TTS 播放默认不并发；开始播报前关闭录音并清空采集状态。
401: - 屏幕刷新不得持有 Camera、Audio 或网络队列锁；显示失败不阻断主数据流。
402: - TTS 使用小块双缓冲边下边播，不要求完整音频一次性装入 SRAM。
403: - 设备原始媒体只驻留 RAM，请求完成、取消或超时后立即释放。
404: - 云端默认不持久化原始媒体；完整文字、表情和语音字幕记录在结果返回后由
405:   设备本地持久化。
406: - 社交模式结束后，本地至少保存标题、正文、完整文字记录、表情记录、语音
407:   字幕、情绪比例、时间和 `record_id`。
408: - 闲时回顾只上传用户按键选中的一条本地记录，不上传其他历史记录。
409: - 闲时助手只能读取显式白名单字段；拼接进 Prompt 前进行长度限制和敏感字段过滤。
410: - 闲时问答内容在本轮播放完成或取消后释放；回顾问答默认不修改原始历史
411:   记录，是否生成新摘要由后续功能决定。
412: - API Key 不进入仓库、日志或结果记录；端云链路使用 TLS 且必须完成证书校验。
413: - 服务日志只记录耗时、大小、错误码和脱敏会话 ID，不记录原图、音频和字幕。
414: 
415: ## 7. 异常与降级
416: 
417: - 网络拥塞：丢弃旧图片，保留音频和结束控制消息，不改变 5 FPS 的采集配置；
418:   若最终记录无法完整返回，则本地不标记为已完成。
419: - 上传失败：单个块最多重试一次；持续失败则停止会话并提示用户。
420: - 无人脸/遮挡/模糊：记录无效原因，不调用大模型强行分类。
421: - ASR 或表情服务失败：最终结果标明缺失模态，不把单一模态包装成联合判断。
422: - 大模型超时或 Schema 非法：返回分析失败，不展示未校验的自由文本。
423: - 设备取消或断开：云端终止在途任务并按 TTL 清理，不在后台持续采集或推理；
424:   已存在的本地历史记录不被删除。
425: - 闲时助手 ASR/模型/TTS 任一环节失败：停止后续步骤并用屏幕和震动提示，
426:   不播放旧会话音频。
427: - TTS 下载中断：停止 DAC、释放部分音频，不将截断内容标记为成功。
428: - 模式切换请求发生在忙状态：先提示用户取消当前任务，不强行抢占共享外设。
429: 
430: ## 8. 场景数据包示例
431: 
432: ### 8.1 通用通信约定
433: 
434: - 设备与统一 AI 接口使用 HTTPS；JSON 使用 `application/json`，JPEG 和音频
435:   使用二进制正文，不进行 Base64 编码。
436: - 每个设备请求携带 `Authorization: Bearer <token>`，但 Token 不出现在正文、
437:   URL、日志和以下示例中。
438: - 社交模式使用 `session_id`，闲时助手使用 `request_id`，本地记录使用
439:   `record_id`。同一 ID 下的 `sequence` 单调递增，重传保持原序号。
440: - `timestamp_ms` 是本次会话或请求开始后的单调时钟毫秒数；需要绝对时间时
441:   另用 ISO 8601 格式的 `created_at`。
442: - 所有二进制包必须使用 `Content-Length`；接收端按长度读取，不能依赖字符串
443:   结束符。服务端同时限制单包长度，超过限制返回 `413 Payload Too Large`。
444: - 成功响应使用 `2xx`；格式错误使用 `400`；鉴权失败使用 `401`；会话不存在
445:   使用 `404`；序号冲突使用 `409`；限流使用 `429`；内部失败使用 `5xx`。
446: 
447: ### 8.2 社交模式：创建会话
448: 
449: 设备在用户确认隐私提示后创建会话：
450: 
451: ```http
452: POST /v1/social/sessions HTTP/1.1
453: Content-Type: application/json
454: 
455: {
456:   "schema_version": "social-session/v1",
457:   "device_id": "vela-264-demo",
458:   "sequence": 1,
459:   "timestamp_ms": 0,
460:   "image": {"format": "image/jpeg", "width": 640, "height": 480, "fps": 5},
461:   "audio": {"format": "audio/pcm", "sample_rate": 16000, "bits": 16, "channels": 1}
462: }
463: ```
464: 
465: 统一 AI 接口返回会话 ID 和服务端限制：
466: 
467: ```http
468: HTTP/1.1 201 Created
469: Content-Type: application/json
470: 
471: {
472:   "schema_version": "social-session/v1",
473:   "session_id": "sess-20260817-0001",
474:   "status": "recording",
475:   "sequence": 1,
476:   "timestamp_ms": 12,
477:   "limits": {
478:     "max_duration_s": 1800,
479:     "max_image_bytes": 163840,
480:     "audio_chunk_ms": 2000
481:   }
482: }
483: ```
484: 
485: ### 8.3 社交模式：JPEG 帧上传
486: 
487: 每个 JPEG 使用原始二进制正文。业务固定 5 FPS，因此相邻帧时间戳通常相差
488: 约 200 ms；网络拥塞时允许序号不连续，云端不得等待已被设备丢弃的旧帧。
489: 
490: ```http
491: POST /v1/social/sessions/sess-20260817-0001/frames HTTP/1.1
492: Content-Type: image/jpeg
493: Content-Length: 30763
494: X-Schema-Version: social-frame/v1
495: X-Sequence: 26
496: X-Timestamp-Ms: 5000
497: X-Width: 640
498: X-Height: 480
499: 
500: <30763 bytes of JPEG data: FF D8 ... FF D9>
501: ```
502: 
503: 服务端只确认接收，不向设备返回小模型内部结果：
504: 
505: ```json
506: {
507:   "schema_version": "social-frame-ack/v1",
508:   "session_id": "sess-20260817-0001",
509:   "sequence": 26,
510:   "timestamp_ms": 5018,
511:   "status": "accepted"
512: }
513: ```
514: 
515: ### 8.4 社交模式：音频分块上传
516: 
517: 示例采用 2 秒裸 PCM：`16000 x 2 bytes x 1 channel x 2 s = 64000 bytes`。
518: 如后续改为 Ogg Opus，仅修改 `Content-Type` 和编码元数据，不改变会话语义。
519: 
520: ```http
521: POST /v1/social/sessions/sess-20260817-0001/audio HTTP/1.1
522: Content-Type: audio/pcm
523: Content-Length: 64000
524: X-Schema-Version: social-audio/v1
525: X-Sequence: 3
526: X-Start-Ms: 4000
527: X-Duration-Ms: 2000
528: X-Sample-Rate: 16000
529: X-Sample-Bits: 16
530: X-Channels: 1
531: 
532: <64000 bytes of little-endian signed PCM>
533: ```
534: 
535: 音频接收响应：
536: 
537: ```json
538: {
539:   "schema_version": "social-audio-ack/v1",
540:   "session_id": "sess-20260817-0001",
541:   "sequence": 3,
542:   "timestamp_ms": 6021,
543:   "status": "accepted"
544: }
545: ```
546: 
547: 云端内部可由该音频生成如下时间线数据，但记录期间不要求逐条下发设备：
548: 
549: ```json
550: {
551:   "start_ms": 5000,
552:   "end_ms": 6200,
553:   "transcript": "我不太明白刚才这一点。",
554:   "emotion": "possible_confusion",
555:   "confidence": 0.78,
556:   "evidence": "multiple_consistent_frames",
557:   "uncertainty": null
558: }
559: ```
560: 
561: ### 8.5 社交模式：即时提示
562: 
563: 云端内部确认持续显著线索后，通过统一接口向设备返回短提示。该包不包含
564: 完整历史，也不结束会话：
565: 
566: ```json
567: {
568:   "schema_version": "social-alert/v1",
569:   "session_id": "sess-20260817-0001",
570:   "sequence": 1,
571:   "timestamp_ms": 8400,
572:   "status": "active",
573:   "cue": "possible_confusion",
574:   "confidence": 0.82,
575:   "display_text": "可能困惑",
576:   "suggestion": "可以放慢语速并确认是否理解。",
577:   "urgency": "normal",
578:   "tts_text": "对方可能有些困惑，可以确认是否需要解释。"
579: }
580: ```
581: 
582: 设备收到后先震动并刷新屏幕，仅在用户确认后将 `tts_text` 送入 TTS。
583: 
584: ### 8.6 社交模式：结束与最终记录
585: 
586: 设备停止 Camera 和 Audio、上传最后一个音频块后发送结束请求：
587: 
588: ```http
589: POST /v1/social/sessions/sess-20260817-0001/finalize HTTP/1.1
590: Content-Type: application/json
591: 
592: {
593:   "schema_version": "social-finalize/v1",
594:   "session_id": "sess-20260817-0001",
595:   "sequence": 1,
596:   "timestamp_ms": 30000,
597:   "last_frame_sequence": 150,
598:   "last_audio_sequence": 15,
599:   "reason": "user_finished"
600: }
601: ```
602: 
603: 若处理尚未完成，服务端先返回异步任务：
604: 
605: ```json
606: {
607:   "schema_version": "social-finalize/v1",
608:   "session_id": "sess-20260817-0001",
609:   "status": "processing",
610:   "result_id": "result-0001",
611:   "sequence": 1,
612:   "timestamp_ms": 30120,
613:   "poll_after_ms": 1000
614: }
615: ```
616: 
617: 设备轮询 `GET /v1/social/results/result-0001` 后得到一次性完整结果：
618: 
619: ```json
620: {
621:   "schema_version": "social-cue/v1",
622:   "session_id": "sess-20260817-0001",
623:   "status": "completed",
624:   "sequence": 2,

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/social_cue/social_cue_main.c
3:  *
4:  * VelaSight's表情线索 state machine, end to end, without the cloud.
5:  *
6:  * What this is for: the plan's week-4 deliverable is the Agent state flow
7:  * idle -> capturing -> analyzing -> notifying -> cancelled plus one Mock
8:  * closed loop, and the risk table's fallback for "Wi-Fi not through yet" is
9:  * exactly this -- demonstrate the flow with a local mock response.  So the
10:  * only mocked step here is the network request.  Everything else is real:
11:  * the frame comes from /dev/video0 through the same V4L2 sequence
12:  * packages/ai_agent's tool_camera.c uses, the confidence policy is the one
13:  * from the skill document, and the haptic output drives /dev/pwm0.
14:  *
15:  * The policy is the point.  A demo that always prints a cheerful verdict
16:  * proves nothing; what has to be visible is the *refusal* path -- low
17:  * confidence, no face, conflicting cues -- because that is what the product
18:  * promises and what a reviewer should be able to trigger on demand.
19:  *
20:  * Usage:
21:  *   social_cue                 one cycle, real capture, mock analysis
22:  *   social_cue case <0..4>     force a specific mock verdict (see below)
23:  *   social_cue mock            skip the camera too (no hardware needed)
24:  *   social_cue schema          print the JSON contract the vision model owes us
25:  *   social_cue install         write the skill document to the agent's skills dir
26:  *   social_cue n=<count>       repeat the cycle
27:  *
28:  * Ctrl-C during capture or analysis takes the cancelled path: the frame is
29:  * released and nothing is reported, which is the privacy requirement rather
30:  * than a nicety.
31:  *
32:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
33:  ****************************************************************************/
34: 
35: /****************************************************************************
36:  * Included Files
37:  ****************************************************************************/
38: 
39: #include <nuttx/config.h>
40: 
41: #include <errno.h>
42: #include <fcntl.h>
43: #include <poll.h>
44: #include <signal.h>
45: #include <stdbool.h>
46: #include <stdio.h>
47: #include <stdlib.h>
48: #include <string.h>
49: #include <sys/ioctl.h>
50: #include <sys/mman.h>
51: #include <sys/stat.h>
52: #include <unistd.h>
53: 
54: #include <nuttx/fs/ioctl.h>
55: #include <nuttx/timers/pwm.h>
56: 
57: #include <sys/videoio.h>
58: 
59: #include "social_cue_skill.h"
60: 
61: /****************************************************************************
62:  * Pre-processor Definitions
63:  ****************************************************************************/
64: 
65: #define SC_VIDEO_DEV      "/dev/video0"
66: #define SC_PWM_DEV        "/dev/pwm0"
67: 
68: /* Where the agent looks for skills.  Kept as a literal rather than including
69:  * the agent's headers: this app must build whether or not ai_agent is in the
70:  * configuration.  It matches CONFIG_EXAMPLES_AI_AGENT_VELA_DATA_DIR.
71:  */
72: 
73: #define SC_SKILLS_DIR     "/mnt/ai_agent/skills"
74: #define SC_SKILL_PATH     SC_SKILLS_DIR "/social-cue-assistant.md"
75: 
76: /* One frame, JPEG.  480x480 is the only geometry this sensor driver offers
77:  * that is square, and sizeimage is what decides the buffer size for a
78:  * compressed format (docs/reference/camera.md 14.2).
79:  */
80: 
81: #define SC_WIDTH          480
82: #define SC_HEIGHT         480
83: #define SC_SIZEIMAGE      (160 * 1024)
84: #define SC_NBUFFERS       2
85: #define SC_CAPTURE_TMO_MS 5000
86: 
87: /* The thresholds from the skill document.  They live here as well because
88:  * this is the code that has to enforce them.
89:  */
90: 
91: #define SC_CONF_REPORT    0.60f
92: #define SC_CONF_WEAK      0.40f
93: #define SC_CONFLICT_CONF  0.60f
94: 
95: /* Haptics.  Three patterns, deliberately distinguishable without looking:
96:  * one short pulse for "capturing", two for "here is a hint", one long for
97:  * "I cannot tell".  1 kHz at 70% duty is what bk7258_motor.c uses.
98:  */
99: 
100: #define SC_MOTOR_FREQ     1000
101: #define SC_MOTOR_DUTY     ((ub16_t)((7u * 65536u) / 10u))
102: 
103: /****************************************************************************
104:  * Private Types
105:  ****************************************************************************/
106: 
107: enum sc_state_e
108: {
109:   SC_IDLE = 0,
110:   SC_CAPTURING,
111:   SC_ANALYZING,
112:   SC_NOTIFYING,
113:   SC_CANCELLED
114: };
115: 
116: /* One cue as the vision model reports it. */
117: 
118: struct sc_cue_s
119: {
120:   const char *cue;        /* observable, e.g. "brow_furrow" */
121:   const char *meaning;    /* hedged reading, e.g. "possible confusion" */
122:   float       confidence;
123: };
124: 
125: /* The whole response.  This mirrors the JSON contract in the skill document;

202: /****************************************************************************
203:  * Name: sc_buzz
204:  *
205:  * Description:
206:  *   Pulse the vibration motor count times.  Best-effort: a board without
207:  *   /dev/pwm0 still runs the state machine, it just says so once.
208:  *
209:  ****************************************************************************/
210: 
211: static void sc_buzz(int count, int on_ms, int off_ms)
212: {
213:   struct pwm_info_s info;
214:   int fd;
215:   int i;
216: 
217:   fd = open(SC_PWM_DEV, O_RDONLY);
218:   if (fd < 0)
219:     {
220:       printf("social_cue: no %s (errno=%d), haptics skipped\n",
221:              SC_PWM_DEV, errno);
222:       return;
223:     }
224: 
225:   memset(&info, 0, sizeof(info));
226:   info.frequency = SC_MOTOR_FREQ;
227:   info.duty      = SC_MOTOR_DUTY;
228: 
229:   if (ioctl(fd, PWMIOC_SETCHARACTERISTICS, (unsigned long)&info) < 0)
230:     {
231:       printf("social_cue: PWMIOC_SETCHARACTERISTICS failed, errno=%d\n",
232:              errno);
233:       close(fd);
234:       return;
235:     }
236: 
237:   for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
238:     {
239:       ioctl(fd, PWMIOC_START, 0);
240:       usleep((useconds_t)on_ms * 1000);
241:       ioctl(fd, PWMIOC_STOP, 0);
242:       if (i + 1 < count)
243:         {
244:           usleep((useconds_t)off_ms * 1000);
245:         }
246:     }
247: 
248:   close(fd);
249: }

251: /****************************************************************************
252:  * Name: sc_capture
253:  *
254:  * Description:
255:  *   Grab one JPEG frame.  Same ioctl order as packages/ai_agent's
256:  *   tool_camera.c: S_FMT -> REQBUFS -> QUERYBUF+mmap -> QBUF -> STREAMON ->
257:  *   poll -> DQBUF.  The bytes are counted and then dropped; nothing here
258:  *   needs the pixels, and keeping them would violate the privacy rule for no
259:  *   benefit.
260:  *
261:  * Returned Value:
262:  *   Frame length in bytes, or a negated errno.
263:  *
264:  ****************************************************************************/
265: 
266: static ssize_t sc_capture(void)
267: {
268:   struct v4l2_requestbuffers req;
269:   struct v4l2_buffer buf;
270:   struct v4l2_format fmt;
271:   struct pollfd pfd;
272:   void *addr[SC_NBUFFERS];
273:   size_t len[SC_NBUFFERS];
274:   ssize_t used = -EIO;
275:   int fd;
276:   int i;
277: 
278:   for (i = 0; i < SC_NBUFFERS; i++)
279:     {
280:       addr[i] = NULL;
281:       len[i]  = 0;
282:     }
283: 
284:   fd = open(SC_VIDEO_DEV, O_RDWR);
285:   if (fd < 0)
286:     {
287:       printf("social_cue: open %s failed, errno=%d\n", SC_VIDEO_DEV, errno);
288:       return -errno;
289:     }
290: 
291:   memset(&fmt, 0, sizeof(fmt));
292:   fmt.type                = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
293:   fmt.fmt.pix.width       = SC_WIDTH;
294:   fmt.fmt.pix.height      = SC_HEIGHT;
295:   fmt.fmt.pix.pixelformat = V4L2_PIX_FMT_JPEG;
296:   fmt.fmt.pix.field       = V4L2_FIELD_ANY;
297:   fmt.fmt.pix.sizeimage   = SC_SIZEIMAGE;
298: 
299:   if (ioctl(fd, VIDIOC_S_FMT, (unsigned long)&fmt) < 0)
300:     {
301:       printf("social_cue: S_FMT JPEG %dx%d failed, errno=%d\n",
302:              SC_WIDTH, SC_HEIGHT, errno);
303:       used = -errno;
304:       goto out;
305:     }
306: 
307:   memset(&req, 0, sizeof(req));
308:   req.type   = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
309:   req.memory = V4L2_MEMORY_MMAP;
310:   req.count  = SC_NBUFFERS;
311: 
312:   if (ioctl(fd, VIDIOC_REQBUFS, (unsigned long)&req) < 0)
313:     {
314:       printf("social_cue: REQBUFS failed, errno=%d\n", errno);
315:       used = -errno;
316:       goto out;
317:     }
318: 
319:   for (i = 0; i < SC_NBUFFERS; i++)
320:     {
321:       memset(&buf, 0, sizeof(buf));
322:       buf.type   = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
323:       buf.memory = V4L2_MEMORY_MMAP;
324:       buf.index  = (uint32_t)i;
325: 
326:       if (ioctl(fd, VIDIOC_QUERYBUF, (unsigned long)&buf) < 0)
327:         {
328:           printf("social_cue: QUERYBUF[%d] failed, errno=%d\n", i, errno);
329:           used = -errno;
330:           goto out;
331:         }
332: 
333:       addr[i] = mmap(NULL, buf.length, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED,
334:                      fd, (off_t)buf.m.offset);
335:       if (addr[i] == MAP_FAILED)
336:         {
337:           addr[i] = NULL;
338:           printf("social_cue: mmap[%d] failed, errno=%d\n", i, errno);
339:           used = -errno;
340:           goto out;
341:         }
342: 
343:       len[i] = buf.length;
344: 
345:       if (ioctl(fd, VIDIOC_QBUF, (unsigned long)&buf) < 0)
346:         {
347:           printf("social_cue: QBUF[%d] failed, errno=%d\n", i, errno);
348:           used = -errno;
349:           goto out;
350:         }
351:     }
352: 
353:   if (ioctl(fd, VIDIOC_STREAMON, (unsigned long)&req.type) < 0)
354:     {
355:       printf("social_cue: STREAMON failed, errno=%d\n", errno);
356:       used = -errno;
357:       goto out;
358:     }
359: 
360:   pfd.fd     = fd;
361:   pfd.events = POLLIN;
362: 
363:   if (poll(&pfd, 1, SC_CAPTURE_TMO_MS) <= 0)
364:     {
365:       printf("social_cue: no frame within %d ms\n", SC_CAPTURE_TMO_MS);
366:       used = -ETIMEDOUT;
367:     }
368:   else
369:     {
370:       memset(&buf, 0, sizeof(buf));
371:       buf.type   = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
372:       buf.memory = V4L2_MEMORY_MMAP;
373: 
374:       if (ioctl(fd, VIDIOC_DQBUF, (unsigned long)&buf) < 0)
375:         {
376:           printf("social_cue: DQBUF failed, errno=%d\n", errno);
377:           used = -errno;
378:         }
379:       else
380:         {
381:           used = (ssize_t)buf.bytesused;
382:         }
383:     }
384: 
385:   ioctl(fd, VIDIOC_STREAMOFF, (unsigned long)&req.type);
386: 
387: out:
388:   for (i = 0; i < SC_NBUFFERS; i++)
389:     {
390:       if (addr[i] != NULL)
391:         {
392:           munmap(addr[i], len[i]);
393:         }
394:     }
395: 
396:   close(fd);
397:   return used;
398: }

400: /****************************************************************************
401:  * Name: sc_print_request / sc_print_response
402:  *
403:  * Description:
404:  *   Show what would go up and what came back.  Printed rather than sent,
405:  *   because the mock is the point -- but printed in the exact shape the real
406:  *   request uses, so the swap is a small diff and a reviewer can see the
407:  *   contract.
408:  *
409:  ****************************************************************************/
410: 
411: static void sc_print_request(ssize_t frame_len)
412: {
413:   printf("social_cue: request  {\"model\":\"vision\",\"image_bytes\":%ld,"
414:          "\"max_cues\":3,\"schema\":\"social-cue/v1\"}\n", (long)frame_len);
415: }
416: 
417: static void sc_print_response(const struct sc_verdict_s *v)
418: {
419:   int i;
420: 
421:   printf("social_cue: response {\"cues\":[");
422:   for (i = 0; i < v->ncues; i++)
423:     {
424:       printf("%s{\"cue\":\"%s\",\"meaning\":\"%s\",\"confidence\":%.2f}",
425:              i ? "," : "", v->cues[i].cue, v->cues[i].meaning,
426:              (double)v->cues[i].confidence);
427:     }
428: 
429:   printf("],\"overall_confidence\":%.2f,\"unable_to_judge\":%s,"
430:          "\"reason\":\"%s\",\"suggestion\":\"%s\"}\n",
431:          (double)v->overall, v->unable ? "true" : "false",
432:          v->reason, v->suggestion);
433: }
434: 
435: /****************************************************************************
436:  * Name: sc_conflicting
437:  *
438:  * Description:
439:  *   Two cues that both read strongly and point in different directions.  The
440:  *   skill document forces "unable to judge" here; without this check the
441:  *   policy would happily report whichever cue the model listed first, which
442:  *   is the failure mode the rule exists to prevent.
443:  *
444:  ****************************************************************************/
445: 
446: static bool sc_conflicting(const struct sc_verdict_s *v)
447: {
448:   int strong = 0;
449:   int i;
450: 
451:   for (i = 0; i < v->ncues; i++)
452:     {
453:       if (v->cues[i].confidence >= SC_CONFLICT_CONF)
454:         {
455:           strong++;
456:         }
457:     }
458: 
459:   return strong >= 2;
460: }
461: 
462: /****************************************************************************
463:  * Name: sc_notify
464:  *
465:  * Description:
466:  *   Apply the confidence policy and produce the wearer-facing line.  This is
467:  *   the whole product logic in one place, on purpose.
468:  *
469:  ****************************************************************************/
470: 
471: static void sc_notify(const struct sc_verdict_s *v)
472: {
473:   if (v->unable)
474:     {
475:       printf("social_cue: SAY  \"看不清表情，判断不了（%s）。\"\n", v->reason);
476:       printf("social_cue: policy unable_to_judge=true reason=%s\n", v->reason);
477:       sc_buzz(1, 400, 0);
478:       return;
479:     }
480: 
481:   if (sc_conflicting(v))
482:     {
483:       printf("social_cue: SAY  \"信号不一致，%s 和 %s 都很明显，直接问一句更稳。\"\n",
484:              v->cues[0].meaning, v->cues[1].meaning);
485:       printf("social_cue: policy conflicting_cues -> withheld a verdict\n");
486:       sc_buzz(1, 400, 0);
487:       return;
488:     }
489: 
490:   if (v->overall < SC_CONF_WEAK)
491:     {
492:       printf("social_cue: SAY  \"没有明显线索，判断不了。\"\n");
493:       printf("social_cue: policy overall=%.2f < %.2f -> unable\n",
494:              (double)v->overall, (double)SC_CONF_WEAK);
495:       sc_buzz(1, 400, 0);
496:       return;
497:     }
498: 
499:   if (v->overall < SC_CONF_REPORT)
500:     {
501:       printf("social_cue: SAY  \"可能有点%s，不过这个判断不太确定。\"\n",
502:              v->cues[0].meaning);
503:       printf("social_cue: policy overall=%.2f in [%.2f,%.2f) -> cue only, "
504:              "no suggestion\n", (double)v->overall,
505:              (double)SC_CONF_WEAK, (double)SC_CONF_REPORT);
506:       sc_buzz(2, 80, 120);
507:       return;
508:     }
509: 
510:   printf("social_cue: SAY  \"他%s（%s，%.0f%%）。建议：%s。\"\n",
511:          v->cues[0].cue, v->cues[0].meaning,
512:          (double)(v->overall * 100.0f), v->suggestion);
513:   printf("social_cue: policy overall=%.2f >= %.2f -> cue + suggestion\n",
514:          (double)v->overall, (double)SC_CONF_REPORT);
515:   sc_buzz(2, 80, 120);
516: }

518: /****************************************************************************
519:  * Name: sc_install_skill
520:  *
521:  * Description:
522:  *   Write the skill document where the agent will read it.  The agent installs
523:  *   its own built-ins but has no idea about this one, and the board has no way
524:  *   to receive a file from the host, so the firmware carries the text.
525:  *
526:  ****************************************************************************/
527: 
528: static int sc_install_skill(void)
529: {
530:   static const char skill[] = SOCIAL_CUE_SKILL_MD;
531:   FILE *f;
532:   size_t n;
533: 
534:   /* The agent creates this tree itself when it starts, but this command has
535:    * to work whether or not it has run yet.
536:    */
537: 
538:   mkdir("/mnt/ai_agent", 0755);
539:   mkdir(SC_SKILLS_DIR, 0755);
540: 
541:   f = fopen(SC_SKILL_PATH, "w");
542:   if (f == NULL)
543:     {
544:       printf("social_cue: cannot write %s (errno=%d).\n",
545:              SC_SKILL_PATH, errno);

557:              SC_SKILL_PATH, n, sizeof(skill) - 1);
558:       return -EIO;

561:   printf("social_cue: installed %s (%zu bytes)\n", SC_SKILL_PATH, n);
562:   printf("social_cue: the agent picks it up on its next prompt build; "
563:          "no restart needed.\n");
564:   return OK;

567: /****************************************************************************
568:  * Name: sc_cycle
569:  ****************************************************************************/
570: 
571: static int sc_cycle(bool real_capture, const struct sc_verdict_s *verdict)
572: {
573:   enum sc_state_e state = SC_IDLE;
574:   ssize_t frame_len = 0;
575: 
576:   g_cancelled = 0;
577: 
578:   sc_enter(&state, SC_CAPTURING);
579:   sc_buzz(1, 60, 0);
580: 
581:   if (real_capture)
582:     {
583:       frame_len = sc_capture();
584:       if (frame_len < 0)
585:         {
586:           printf("social_cue: capture failed (%d); no verdict, nothing "
587:                  "retained\n", (int)frame_len);
588:           sc_enter(&state, SC_IDLE);
589:           return (int)frame_len;
590:         }
591: 
592:       printf("social_cue: captured %ld bytes, JPEG %dx%d\n",
593:              (long)frame_len, SC_WIDTH, SC_HEIGHT);
594:     }
595:   else
596:     {
597:       frame_len = 41984;
598:       printf("social_cue: mock frame, %ld bytes (camera not touched)\n",
599:              (long)frame_len);
600:     }
601: 
602:   if (g_cancelled)
603:     {
604:       sc_enter(&state, SC_CANCELLED);
605:       printf("social_cue: cancelled during capture; frame released, "
606:              "nothing reported\n");
607:       return OK;
608:     }
609: 
610:   sc_enter(&state, SC_ANALYZING);
611:   sc_print_request(frame_len);
612: 
613:   /* Where the HTTPS request goes.  Until then, a fixed response and a pause
614:    * long enough that the cancelled path is reachable by hand.
615:    */
616: 
617:   usleep(300 * 1000);
618: 
619:   if (g_cancelled)
620:     {
621:       sc_enter(&state, SC_CANCELLED);
622:       printf("social_cue: cancelled during analysis; result discarded\n");
623:       return OK;
624:     }
625: 
626:   sc_print_response(verdict);
627: 
628:   sc_enter(&state, SC_NOTIFYING);
629:   sc_notify(verdict);
630: 
631:   sc_enter(&state, SC_IDLE);
632:   printf("social_cue: frame released, no media or verdict retained\n");
633:   return OK;
634: }

636: /****************************************************************************
637:  * Name: sc_usage
638:  ****************************************************************************/

640: static void sc_usage(void)
641: {
642:   printf("Usage: social_cue [mock] [case <0..%u>] [n=<count>] "
643:          "[schema|install]\n", (unsigned int)SC_NMOCKS - 1);
644:   printf("  (no args)   one cycle: real capture, mock analysis\n");
645:   printf("  mock        skip the camera as well\n");
646:   printf("  case <n>    0 clear  1 weak  2 below floor  3 no face  "
647:          "4 conflicting\n");
648:   printf("  n=<count>   repeat the cycle\n");
649:   printf("  schema      print the JSON contract\n");
650:   printf("  install     write the skill document to %s\n", SC_SKILL_PATH);
651:   printf("Ctrl-C during capture or analysis takes the cancelled path.\n");
652: }

654: /****************************************************************************
655:  * Public Functions
656:  ****************************************************************************/
657: 
658: int main(int argc, char *argv[])
659: {
660:   struct sigaction act;
661:   const struct sc_verdict_s *verdict = &g_mock_cases[0];
662:   bool real_capture = true;
663:   int count = 1;
664:   int i;
665:   int ret = OK;
666: 
667:   for (i = 1; i < argc; i++)
668:     {
669:       if (strcmp(argv[i], "mock") == 0)
670:         {
671:           real_capture = false;
672:         }
673:       else if (strcmp(argv[i], "case") == 0 && i + 1 < argc)
674:         {
675:           int n = atoi(argv[++i]);
676:           if (n < 0 || n >= (int)SC_NMOCKS)
677:             {
678:               printf("social_cue: case must be 0..%u\n",
679:                      (unsigned int)SC_NMOCKS - 1);
680:               return 1;
681:             }
682: 
683:           verdict = &g_mock_cases[n];
684:         }
685:       else if (strncmp(argv[i], "n=", 2) == 0)
686:         {
687:           count = atoi(argv[i] + 2);
688:           if (count < 1)
689:             {
690:               count = 1;
691:             }
692:         }
693:       else if (strcmp(argv[i], "schema") == 0)
694:         {
695:           printf("social-cue/v1:\n"
696:                  "{\n"
697:                  "  \"cues\": [ { \"cue\": \"brow_furrow\","
698:                  " \"meaning\": \"possible confusion\","
699:                  " \"confidence\": 0.72 } ],\n"
700:                  "  \"overall_confidence\": 0.72,\n"
701:                  "  \"unable_to_judge\": false,\n"
702:                  "  \"reason\": \"\",\n"
703:                  "  \"suggestion\": \"slow down and check\"\n"
704:                  "}\n"
705:                  "thresholds: >=%.2f cue+suggestion, >=%.2f cue only, "
706:                  "else unable\n"
707:                  "forced unable: no_face, face_too_small, conflicting_cues\n",
708:                  (double)SC_CONF_REPORT, (double)SC_CONF_WEAK);
709:           return 0;
710:         }
711:       else if (strcmp(argv[i], "install") == 0)
712:         {
713:           return sc_install_skill() == OK ? 0 : 1;
714:         }
715:       else
716:         {
717:           sc_usage();
718:           return 1;
719:         }
720:     }
721: 
722:   /* Ctrl-C has to reach this task for the cancelled path to be demonstrable.
723:    * NSH does not always claim the console for a builtin on this board (see
724:    * app/camera_preview's note), but installing a handler is what makes the
725:    * signal actionable rather than fatal.
726:    */
727: 
728:   memset(&act, 0, sizeof(act));
729:   act.sa_handler = sc_sigint;
730:   sigaction(SIGINT, &act, NULL);
731: 
732:   for (i = 0; i < count && ret == OK; i++)
733:     {
734:       if (count > 1)
735:         {
736:           printf("social_cue: --- cycle %d/%d ---\n", i + 1, count);
737:         }
738: 
739:       ret = sc_cycle(real_capture, verdict);
740:     }
741: 
742:   return ret == OK ? 0 : 1;
743: }

1: /****************************************************************************

3:  *
4:  * Live camera preview: GC2145 (640x480 packed 4:2:2, V Y1 U Y0 in memory)
5:  * -> GC9D01 (160x160 RGB565), pushed to every registered panel.
6:  *
7:  * Why this exists instead of `nxcamera; output /dev/fb0`: nxcamera's
8:  * show_image() passes the camera's own width and height as both source and
9:  * crop rectangle and gives libyuv only the framebuffer's stride, so it
10:  * would write a 640x480 image into a 160x160 framebuffer and run off the
11:  * end of it; and for a non-I420 source on an RGB565 panel it allocates
12:  * width*height*3/2 (460800 bytes) from the kernel heap, which on this board
13:  * holds roughly 300KB.  nxcamera also lives in the shared apps repository,
14:  * outside this project's scope, so it is left alone.
15:  *
16:  * Conversion: a single pass that samples the source directly into the
17:  * framebuffer, with no intermediate buffer at all.
18:  *
19:  *   centre-crop 480x480 out of 640x480, then take every 3rd pixel
20:  *   (480 / 160 == 3 exactly, so nearest-neighbour needs no arithmetic
21:  *   beyond an integer stride) and convert that chroma/luma group to RGB565.
22:  *
23:  * Going through libyuv would have meant staging I420 at crop size
24:  * (480*480*3/2 = 345600 bytes) and again at panel size, i.e. exactly the
25:  * allocation that defeats nxcamera on this board.  Sampling directly also
26:  * reads only ~100KB of the 614400-byte source frame per displayed frame,
27:  * which matters because PSRAM bandwidth is already the tightest resource
28:  * here (the capture path alone runs at ~37MB/s).
29:  *
30:  * The centre crop is what keeps the picture from being stretched: the panel
31:  * is a 160x160 round display, so a 4:3 frame is cropped to its central
32:  * square first.  The corners of that square are not visible on a round
33:  * panel -- that is a composition matter, not something this code hides.
34:  *
35:  * Dual panel: the board drives two GC9D01 screens (/dev/fb0 and /dev/fb1).
36:  * Conversion runs once into the first framebuffer and the result is copied
37:  * to the others, since both eyes show the same image.  The copy is 51200
38:  * bytes of kernel RAM, far cheaper than converting twice.  Each panel is
39:  * then pushed independently; at ~27ms per panel per frame the bus, not the
40:  * conversion, is the frame-rate limit.
41:  *
42:  * Usage:
43:  *   camera_preview [N] [options]        live preview, N frames (0 = forever)
44:  *   camera_preview live+face [N] [expr=<name>] [cycle=<sec>]
45:  *                                       fb0 live at the camera's full rate,
46:  *                                       fb1 an expression, repainted only
47:  *                                       when it changes

60:  *                           same form agent_camera uses, so
61:  *                           tools/b64frames.py rebuilds it without any

357:  ****************************************************************************/
358: 
359: /* Set from the SIGINT handler; the capture loop polls it.
360:  *
361:  * Live preview has no frame limit (`camera_preview` with no count runs until
362:  * stopped), so Ctrl-C is the only way out, and simply being killed is not
363:  * good enough: the exit path has to reach preview_cleanup(), which issues
364:  * VIDIOC_STREAMOFF, munmaps the buffers and releases them with REQBUFS(0).
365:  * Skipping that leaves the sensor streaming and the PSRAM buffer heap
366:  * allocated -- and that heap is larger than the AP's whole kernel heap.
367:  *
368:  * Two things are needed for Ctrl-C to arrive at all, and both were missing
369:  * before: CONFIG_TTY_SIGINT (which was set) delivers SIGINT to the pid NSH
370:  * registers with TIOCSCTTY, and CONFIG_SIG_DEFAULT (which was NOT set)
371:  * supplies the default action.  Without the latter a process that installs
372:  * no handler simply ignores the signal, which is why an earlier Ctrl-C probe
373:  * (app/ctrlc_test) appeared to work -- it installs a handler --
374:  * while this loop did not.  Installing a handler here means the exit no
375:  * longer depends on that config at all.
376:  */
377: 
378: static volatile sig_atomic_t g_stop;
379: static bool g_ctty_claimed;
380: 
381: static void preview_sigint(int signo)
382: {
383:   (void)signo;
384:   g_stop = 1;
385: }
386: 
387: /****************************************************************************
388:  * Name: preview_claim_ctty
389:  *
390:  * Description:
391:  *   Registers this task as the console's controlling terminal, so that a
392:  *   0x03 on the wire turns into a SIGINT delivered here.
393:  *
394:  *   This is not something an application would normally have to do -- NSH is
395:  *   supposed to do it for the foreground task (nsh_builtin.c calls
396:  *   TIOCSCTTY with the child pid before waitpid).  On this board it does not
397:  *   happen: measured with app/ctrlc_test's probe, TIOCSCTTY from inside a
398:  *   freshly started builtin returns 0, i.e. the terminal was still
399:  *   *unclaimed*.  uart_check_special() requires dev->pid > 0, so without
400:  *   this call no amount of Ctrl-C produces a signal, which is exactly why
401:  *   the preview could not be stopped.  Why NSH skips it is still open; the
402:  *   probe reports it in one line and is worth re-running after any NSH or
403:  *   serial change.
404:  *
405:  *   Claiming it also has to be undone (preview_release_ctty), because
406:  *   drivers/serial/serial.c refuses to move an already-set owner: a second
407:  *   TIOCSCTTY returns -EINVAL.  Leaving it set would point SIGINT at a dead
408:  *   pid and break the *next* run.
409:  *
410:  ****************************************************************************/
411: 
412: static void preview_claim_ctty(void)
413: {
414:   if (ioctl(STDIN_FILENO, TIOCSCTTY, (unsigned long)getpid()) == 0)
415:     {
416:       g_ctty_claimed = true;
417:     }
418:   else if (errno != EINVAL)
419:     {
420:       printf("preview: TIOCSCTTY failed: %d (Ctrl-C may not work)\n", errno);
421:     }
422: }
423: 
424: static void preview_release_ctty(void)
425: {
426:   if (g_ctty_claimed)
427:     {
428:       ioctl(STDIN_FILENO, TIOCNOTTY, 0);
429:       g_ctty_claimed = false;
430:     }
431: }
432: 
433: /****************************************************************************
434:  * Name: preview_print_b64
435:  *
436:  * Description:
437:  *   Emit an encoded frame on the console in the same fenced base64 form
438:  *   agent_camera uses, so tools/b64frames.py rebuilds either one and the two
439:  *   paths can be compared byte for byte.  It exists here because the two
440:  *   paths do not agree: the hardware JPEG path (agent_camera, /dev/video0 in
441:  *   JPEG mode) mis-assembles its bitstream -- consecutive frames of a static
442:  *   scene came back differing by 50 to 140 grey levels, the tail of each
443:  *   picture belonging to a different frame, while every marker check passed
444:  *   -- whereas this path encodes a frame that came through the verified UYVY
445:  *   capture, so it is the one to trust for evidence.
446:  *
447:  ****************************************************************************/
448: 
449: static void preview_print_b64(FAR const uint8_t *data, size_t len)
450: {
451:   static const char tbl[] =
452:     "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
453:   uint32_t hash = 2166136261u;
454:   size_t i;
455: 
456:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
457:     {
458:       hash ^= data[i];
459:       hash *= 16777619u;
460:     }
461: 
462:   printf("agent_camera: payload len=%zu fnv1a=0x%08" PRIx32 "\n", len, hash);
463:   printf("-----BEGIN AGENT_CAMERA JPEG %zu-----\n", len);
464: 
465:   for (i = 0; i < len; i += 3)
466:     {
467:       size_t remain = len - i;
468:       uint32_t v = (uint32_t)data[i] << 16;
469:       char quad[4];
470: 
471:       if (remain > 1)
472:         {
473:           v |= (uint32_t)data[i + 1] << 8;
474:         }
475: 
476:       if (remain > 2)
477:         {
478:           v |= data[i + 2];
479:         }
480: 
481:       quad[0] = tbl[(v >> 18) & 0x3f];
482:       quad[1] = tbl[(v >> 12) & 0x3f];
483:       quad[2] = remain > 1 ? tbl[(v >> 6) & 0x3f] : '=';
484:       quad[3] = remain > 2 ? tbl[v & 0x3f] : '=';
485: 
486:       fwrite(quad, 1, 4, stdout);
487: 
488:       if ((i / 3) % 19 == 18)
489:         {
490:           putchar('\n');
491: 
492:           /* Same throttle as agent_camera_print_b64(), and for the same
493:            * reason: the AP's console is a mailbox bridge holding 1024 bytes,
494:            * and an unthrottled 33KB burst arrives truncated -- measured
495:            * 2026-08-17, a 12-frame dump came back with 2 of 12 fences intact
496:            * and both bodies short.  Pausing every two lines keeps the writer
497:            * under the bridge's drain rate.
498:            */
499: 
500:           if (((i / 3) / 19) % 2 == 1)
501:             {
502:               fflush(stdout);
503:               usleep(30000);
504:             }
505:         }
506:     }
507: 
508:   putchar('\n');
509:   printf("-----END AGENT_CAMERA JPEG-----\n");
510: }
511: 
512: static uint32_t now_ms(void)
513: {
514:   struct timespec ts;
515: 
516:   clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
517:   return (uint32_t)(ts.tv_sec * 1000 + ts.tv_nsec / 1000000);
518: }

520: static int preview_open_fb(FAR struct preview_s *p, int want)
521: {
522:   int display;
523: 
524:   for (display = 0; display < MAX_FB; display++)
525:     {
526:       char path[16];
527:       int fd;
528: 
529:       if (want >= 0 && want != display)
530:         {
531:           continue;
532:         }
533: 
534:       snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/dev/fb%d", display);
535: 
536:       fd = open(path, O_RDWR);
537:       if (fd < 0)
538:         {
539:           /* A panel that is not registered is not an error when asking for
540:            * "both" -- a single-panel board is a legitimate configuration.
541:            */
542: 
543:           if (want < 0)
544:             {
545:               continue;
546:             }
547: 
548:           printf("preview: open %s failed: %d\n", path, errno);
549:           return -errno;
550:         }
551: 
552:       if (p->nfb == 0)
553:         {
554:           if (ioctl(fd, FBIOGET_VIDEOINFO, (uintptr_t)&p->vinfo) < 0 ||
555:               ioctl(fd, FBIOGET_PLANEINFO, (uintptr_t)&p->pinfo) < 0)
556:             {
557:               printf("preview: fb%d info ioctl failed: %d\n", display,
558:                      errno);
559:               close(fd);
560:               return -errno;
561:             }
562: 
563:           if (p->vinfo.fmt != FB_FMT_RGB16_565)
564:             {
565:               printf("preview: only RGB565 panels are supported (fmt=%u)\n",
566:                      p->vinfo.fmt);
567:               close(fd);
568:               return -ENOTSUP;
569:             }
570:         }
571: 
572:       p->fbmem[p->nfb] = mmap(NULL, p->pinfo.fblen,
573:                               PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
574:                               MAP_SHARED | MAP_FILE, fd, 0);
575:       if (p->fbmem[p->nfb] == MAP_FAILED)
576:         {
577:           printf("preview: fb%d mmap failed: %d\n", display, errno);
578:           close(fd);
579:           return -errno;
580:         }
581: 
582:       p->fbfd[p->nfb] = fd;
583:       p->fbidx[p->nfb] = display;
584:       p->nfb++;
585:     }
586: 
587:   if (p->nfb == 0)
588:     {
589:       printf("preview: no framebuffer could be opened\n");
590:       return -ENODEV;
591:     }
592: 
593:   /* Default: the live loop owns every panel it opened.  live+face narrows it
594:    * afterwards.
595:    */
596: 
597:   p->npreview = p->nfb;
598: 
599:   printf("preview: %d panel(s), %ux%u fmt=%u bpp=%u stride=%u fblen=%u\n",
600:          p->nfb, p->vinfo.xres, p->vinfo.yres, p->vinfo.fmt,
601:          p->pinfo.bpp, (unsigned int)p->pinfo.stride,
602:          (unsigned int)p->pinfo.fblen);
603: 
604:   return OK;
605: }

607: static int preview_open_camera(FAR struct preview_s *p)
608: {
609:   struct v4l2_requestbuffers req;
610:   struct v4l2_buffer buf;
611:   struct v4l2_format fmt;
612:   int i;
613: 
614:   p->camfd = open(CAM_DEV, O_RDWR);
615:   if (p->camfd < 0)
616:     {
617:       printf("preview: open %s failed: %d\n", CAM_DEV, errno);
618:       return -errno;
619:     }
620: 
621:   memset(&fmt, 0, sizeof(fmt));
622:   fmt.type                = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
623:   fmt.fmt.pix.width       = CAM_WIDTH;
624:   fmt.fmt.pix.height      = CAM_HEIGHT;
625:   fmt.fmt.pix.field       = V4L2_FIELD_ANY;
626: 
627:   /* The real memory layout is V Y1 U Y0 (see preview_convert()), which no
628:    * V4L2 fourcc names: VYUY gets the chroma right but not the reversed luma
629:    * pair, and the imgsensor/imgdata layers this driver sits on define only
630:    * UYVY and YUYV anyway.  UYVY is therefore what both sides agree to call
631:    * it -- a label for "packed 4:2:2, chroma first", with the exact order
632:    * documented in the driver and decoded by preview_convert().  Agreeing
633:    * with the driver is necessary (VIDIOC_S_FMT fails otherwise) but not
634:    * sufficient: both sides can be wrong in the same direction without any
635:    * layer complaining, which is how the chroma swap survived this long.
636:    */
637: 
638:   fmt.fmt.pix.pixelformat = V4L2_PIX_FMT_UYVY;
639: 
640:   if (ioctl(p->camfd, VIDIOC_S_FMT, (uintptr_t)&fmt) < 0)
641:     {
642:       printf("preview: VIDIOC_S_FMT failed: %d\n", errno);
643:       return -errno;
644:     }
645: 
646:   memset(&req, 0, sizeof(req));
647:   req.type   = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
648:   req.memory = V4L2_MEMORY_MMAP;
649:   req.count  = NBUFFERS;
650: 
651:   if (ioctl(p->camfd, VIDIOC_REQBUFS, (uintptr_t)&req) < 0)
652:     {
653:       printf("preview: VIDIOC_REQBUFS failed: %d\n", errno);
654:       return -errno;
655:     }
656: 
657:   p->nbuffers = req.count < NBUFFERS ? req.count : NBUFFERS;
658: 
659:   for (i = 0; i < p->nbuffers; i++)
660:     {
661:       memset(&buf, 0, sizeof(buf));
662:       buf.type   = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
663:       buf.memory = V4L2_MEMORY_MMAP;
664:       buf.index  = i;
665: 
666:       if (ioctl(p->camfd, VIDIOC_QUERYBUF, (uintptr_t)&buf) < 0)
667:         {
668:           printf("preview: VIDIOC_QUERYBUF(%d) failed: %d\n", i, errno);
669:           return -errno;
670:         }
671: 
672:       p->bufs[i] = mmap(NULL, buf.length, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
673:                         MAP_SHARED, p->camfd, buf.m.offset);
674:       if (p->bufs[i] == MAP_FAILED)
675:         {
676:           printf("preview: buffer %d mmap failed: %d\n", i, errno);
677:           return -errno;
678:         }
679: 
680:       p->buf_sizes[i] = buf.length;
681: 
682:       if (ioctl(p->camfd, VIDIOC_QBUF, (uintptr_t)&buf) < 0)
683:         {
684:           printf("preview: VIDIOC_QBUF(%d) failed: %d\n", i, errno);
685:           return -errno;
686:         }
687:     }
688: 
689:   printf("preview: camera %dx%d 4:2:2 (V4L2 tag UYVY, memory V Y1 U Y0), "
690:          "%d buffers of %u bytes\n",
691:          CAM_WIDTH, CAM_HEIGHT, p->nbuffers,
692:          (unsigned int)p->buf_sizes[0]);
693: 
694:   return OK;
695: }

697: /****************************************************************************
698:  * Name: preview_draw_pattern
699:  *
700:  * Description:
701:  *   Static self-test patterns, drawn straight into the framebuffer and
702:  *   pushed once.  These exist to split "the panel shows nothing
703:  *   recognisable" into independent questions without a re-flash per
704:  *   hypothesis:
705:  *
706:  *     fill <hex>  uniform colour.  If this is uniform on the glass, the
707:  *                 transport is sound and any remaining fault is format or
708:  *                 geometry.  If it is uniform but the WRONG colour, it is
709:  *                 byte order.  If it is noise, the transport itself drops
710:  *                 or reorders bytes.
711:  *     pattern     four quadrants + black border.  Colour error, stride
712:  *                 error and window error each look different here, so one
713:  *                 look tells you which of the three it is.
714:  *     bars        8 vertical colour bars.  A single dropped byte shears
715:  *                 every bar below the drop, which a uniform fill hides.
716:  *     grid        1-pixel checkerboard, the worst case for the bus: any
717:  *                 dropped or duplicated word turns the regular lattice
718:  *                 into visible diagonal banding.
719:  *
720:  *   Appending "swap" writes each pixel pre-byte-swapped, which cancels the
721:  *   driver's own swap.  That makes the wire byte order testable from user
722:  *   space: exactly one of `fill f800` and `fill f800 swap` shows red.
723:  *
724:  ****************************************************************************/
725: 
726: static uint16_t preview_pat_bar(int i)
727: {
728:   static const uint16_t bars[8] =
729:   {
730:     0x0000, 0x001f, 0x07e0, 0x07ff, 0xf800, 0xf81f, 0xffe0, 0xffff
731:   };
732: 
733:   return bars[i & 7];
734: }
735: 
736: static int preview_draw_pattern(FAR struct preview_s *p, int argc,
737:                                 FAR char *argv[])
738: {
739:   FAR const char *what = argv[1];
740:   int dw = p->vinfo.xres;
741:   int dh = p->vinfo.yres;
742:   bool swap = false;
743:   uint16_t colour = 0xf800;
744:   int ox = ((g_xoff % dw) + dw) % dw;
745:   int oy = ((g_yoff % dh) + dh) % dh;
746: 
747:   int x;
748:   int y;
749:   int i;
750: 
751:   for (i = 2; i < argc; i++)
752:     {
753:       if (strcmp(argv[i], "swap") == 0)
754:         {
755:           swap = true;
756:         }
757:       else if (strncmp(argv[i], "fb=", 3) != 0 &&
758:                strncmp(argv[i], "sat=", 4) != 0 &&
759:                strncmp(argv[i], "gain=", 5) != 0 &&
760:                strncmp(argv[i], "gamma=", 6) != 0 &&
761:                strncmp(argv[i], "xoff=", 5) != 0 &&
762:                strncmp(argv[i], "yoff=", 5) != 0 &&
763:                strcmp(argv[i], "mx") != 0 &&
764:                strcmp(argv[i], "my") != 0 &&
765:                strcmp(argv[i], "rot180") != 0 &&
766:                strncmp(argv[i], "rgain=", 6) != 0 &&
767:                strncmp(argv[i], "ggain=", 6) != 0 &&
768:                strncmp(argv[i], "bgain=", 6) != 0)
769:         {
770:           colour = (uint16_t)strtoul(argv[i], NULL, 16);
771:         }
772:     }
773: 
774:   for (y = 0; y < dh; y++)
775:     {
776:       int ty = y + oy;
777:       FAR uint16_t *drow;
778: 
779:       if (ty >= dh)
780:         {
781:           ty -= dh;
782:         }
783: 
784:       if (g_mirror_y)
785:         {
786:           ty = dh - 1 - ty;
787:         }
788: 
789:       drow = (FAR uint16_t *)(p->fbmem[0] + (size_t)ty * p->pinfo.stride);
790: 
791:       for (x = 0; x < dw; x++)
792:         {
793:           int tx = x + ox;
794:           uint16_t c;
795: 
796:           if (tx >= dw)
797:             {
798:               tx -= dw;
799:             }
800: 
801:           if (g_mirror_x)
802:             {
803:               tx = dw - 1 - tx;
804:             }
805: 
806:           if (strcmp(what, "fill") == 0)
807:             {
808:               c = colour;
809:             }
810:           else if (strcmp(what, "bars") == 0)
811:             {
812:               c = preview_pat_bar(x * 8 / dw);
813:             }
814:           else if (strcmp(what, "grid") == 0)
815:             {
816:               c = ((x ^ y) & 1) ? 0xffff : 0x0000;
817:             }
818:           else if (strcmp(what, "ruler") == 0)
819:             {
820:               /* Edge markers that make a shift readable by eye.  Each edge
821:                * gets its own colour, so wherever the white band appears is
822:                * where the driver's column 0 actually lands on the glass, and
823:                * the yellow centre line says whether the shift is half a
824:                * screen (the "seam down the middle" case) or something else.
825:                *
826:                *   white  x = 0..3      left edge
827:                *   red    x = 156..159  right edge
828:                *   green  y = 0..3      top edge
829:                *   blue   y = 156..159  bottom edge
830:                *   yellow x = 80        centre
831:                */
832: 
833:               if (x < 4)
834:                 {
835:                   c = 0xffff;                    /* white  */
836:                 }
837:               else if (x >= dw - 4)
838:                 {
839:                   c = 0xf800;                    /* red    */
840:                 }
841:               else if (y < 4)
842:                 {
843:                   c = 0x07e0;                    /* green  */
844:                 }
845:               else if (y >= dh - 4)
846:                 {
847:                   c = 0x001f;                    /* blue   */
848:                 }
849:               else if (x == dw / 2)
850:                 {
851:                   c = 0xffe0;                    /* yellow */
852:                 }
853:               else
854:                 {
855:                   c = 0x0000;
856:                 }
857:             }
858:           else if (strcmp(what, "wb") == 0)
859:             {
860:               /* White-balance ladder: five horizontal bands, each showing
861:                * white (left half) and yellow (right half) with G and B
862:                * progressively attenuated.  Pick the band that looks most
863:                * neutral / most yellow and use its percentage as ggain and
864:                * bgain for the live path.
865:                *
866:                * Attenuating G and B rather than boosting R is deliberate:
867:                * white is 0xFFFF, so R is already at its maximum 31 and
868:                * cannot be raised.  A multiplicative correction can only
869:                * bring the other channels down.
870:                *
871:                * Bands top to bottom: 100%, 92%, 84%, 76%, 68%.
872:                */
873: 
874:               static const int gb[5] =
875:               {
876:                 100, 92, 84, 76, 68
877:               };
878: 
879:               int band = y * 5 / dh;
880:               int k = gb[band > 4 ? 4 : band];
881:               int rr = 31;
882:               int gg = 63 * k / 100;
883:               int bb = (x < dw / 2) ? (31 * k / 100) : 0;
884: 
885:               c = (uint16_t)((rr << 11) | (gg << 5) | bb);
886:             }
887:           else /* "pattern" */
888:             {
889:               if (x < 4 || y < 4 || x >= dw - 4 || y >= dh - 4)
890:                 {
891:                   c = 0x0000;
892:                 }
893:               else if (y < dh / 2)
894:                 {
895:                   c = (x < dw / 2) ? 0xf800 : 0x07e0;
896:                 }
897:               else
898:                 {
899:                   c = (x < dw / 2) ? 0x001f : 0xffff;
900:                 }
901:             }
902: 
903:           drow[tx] = swap ? (uint16_t)((c >> 8) | (c << 8)) : c;
904:         }
905:     }
906: 
907:   for (i = 1; i < p->nfb; i++)
908:     {
909:       memcpy(p->fbmem[i], p->fbmem[0], p->pinfo.fblen);
910:     }
911: 
912:   printf("preview: drew '%s'%s on %dx%d, %d panel(s), xoff=%d yoff=%d "
913:          "mirror=%s%s\n", what, swap ? " (pre-swapped)" : "", dw, dh,
914:          p->nfb, ox, oy, g_mirror_x ? "X" : "-", g_mirror_y ? "Y" : "-");
915: 
916:   return OK;
917: }

919: /****************************************************************************
920:  * Name: preview_convert
921:  *
922:  * Description:
923:  *   One frame: centre-crop, 3:1 nearest-neighbour downscale and packed
924:  *   4:2:2 YUV to RGB565, straight from the capture buffer into the first
925:  *   framebuffer.  BT.601 coefficients in 8-bit fixed point; the shifts are
926:  *   chosen so the whole conversion stays in 32-bit integer math.
927:  *
928:  *   Byte order is V Y1 U Y0: each 4-byte group carries two pixels, with the
929:  *   chroma pair shared between them, but *reversed* -- byte 0 is Cr, byte 2
930:  *   is Cb, and byte 3 is the luma of the left (even) column while byte 1 is
931:  *   the luma of the right (odd) one.  A source x therefore maps to group
932:  *   (x >> 1) and picks byte 3 or byte 1 by x's parity.
933:  *
934:  *   How that was settled.  Three claims have to be separated, and each has
935:  *   its own evidence:
936:  *
937:  *   (1) Which bytes are luma.  Bytes 1 and 3.  Decoding with luma at bytes
938:  *       0/2 was photographed on the panel and gave a geometrically correct,
939:  *       clearly recognisable picture in which every pixel was either
940:  *       saturated green or magenta.  That is the arithmetic signature of
941:  *       feeding chroma into the luma term: with y_code == (U-16)*298 ≈ 33376
942:  *       constant and u_code == v_code == Y-128 == t,
943:  *
944:  *           r = (33376 + 409t) >> 8 = 130 + 1.6t
945:  *           g = (33376 - 308t) >> 8 = 130 - 1.2t
946:  *           b = (33376 + 516t) >> 8 = 130 + 2.0t
947:  *
948:  *       so t < 0 (dark) drives green and t > 0 (bright) drives magenta while
949:  *       luma structure survives, because t still carries it.  A captured
950:  *       frame agrees: over /tmp/frame.yuv, bytes 1 and 3 have sd 39 and span
951:  *       18..153, bytes 0 and 2 have sd 6.2 and 2.3 around 128.
952:  *
953:  *   (2) In which order the two luma samples sit.  Reversed: byte 3 is the
954:  *       left pixel.  Natural images are equally smooth across every pixel
955:  *       boundary, so mean |dY| between the two samples *inside* a group must
956:  *       match mean |dY| *across* the group boundary.  On the captured frame
957:  *       it does not: 1.752 inside versus 3.787 across, a factor of 2.16.
958:  *       Un-swapping the two luma bytes makes it 1.752 versus 1.760 -- and
959:  *       1.76 is also what the same measurement gives vertically (1.621),
960:  *       where no byte ordering is involved.  The asymmetry is the fingerprint
961:  *       of a pair read out backwards: the "across" difference then spans
962:  *       three columns instead of one.
963:  *
964:  *   (3) Which chroma byte is Cb.  Byte 2.  This follows from (2) once the
965:  *       sensor's bus order is known.  The GC2145 is configured with register
966:  *       0x84 = 0x02 (dvp_gc2145.c, commented "yuyv"), which the part's
967:  *       output-format table defines as Y Cb Y Cr on the wire -- corroborated
968:  *       by Zephyr's driver, where VIDEO_PIX_FMT_YUYV maps to
969:  *       GC2145_REG_OUTPUT_FMT_YCBYCR = 0x02.  A group in memory whose luma
970:  *       samples are reversed *and* whose chroma sits at bytes 0/2 is exactly
971:  *       the four bus bytes stored backwards: Y0 Cb Y1 Cr -> Cr Y1 Cb Y0.
972:  *       So byte 0 is Cr and byte 2 is Cb.  Scene evidence agrees: on
973:  *       frame.yuv (red text on a white sign) the extreme chroma deviations
974:  *       are byte0 +57 and byte2 -18, a ratio of -3.17, against -2.96
975:  *       predicted for pure red read as (Cr, Cb) -- and a poor match for blue
976:  *       read the other way round (-6.2 predicted).
977:  *
978:  *   What this fixed.  The decode used to assume plain UYVY (Cb at byte 0),
979:  *   which swaps Cb and Cr and so rotates every hue about the red/blue axis:
980:  *   structure, brightness and grey balance all stay right, which is why the
981:  *   symptom was only "colours a bit off" rather than an obviously broken
982:  *   image.  Reds came out blue.  The luma pair order was wrong at the same
983:  *   time, but that only misplaces detail by one source column and is
984:  *   invisible after the 3:1 downscale.
985:  *
986:  *   Note the layout is not any V4L2 fourcc: VYUY would describe the chroma
987:  *   correctly but not the reversed luma pair.  The driver still advertises
988:  *   V4L2_PIX_FMT_UYVY because that is the closest order the imgsensor and
989:  *   imgdata layers define; see bk7258_camera_imgsensor.c.
990:  *
991:  *   Saturation: with the chroma decoded correctly `camera_preview stats`
992:  *   measures a normal chroma swing (mean |U-128| = 11 on a saturated scene,
993:  *   1 on a grey one), so no correction is applied by default.  g_sat,
994:  *   g_gain, g_full_range and g_uv_swap remain as knobs because colour is
995:  *   subjective and needs the real panel in the loop.
996:  *
997:  ****************************************************************************/

999: /* One source row's worth of the cropped region, staged in SRAM.
1000:  *
1001:  * Why this exists: the capture buffer is in PSRAM, mapped non-cacheable, and
1002:  * a single CPU read of it costs on the order of microseconds.  Measured:
1003:  * converting one 160x160 frame with per-pixel reads straight out of PSRAM
1004:  * took 194ms, i.e. ~7.6us per output pixel -- about 2400 CPU cycles at
1005:  * 320MHz for what is a load plus a dozen arithmetic instructions.  Reducing
1006:  * the number of reads per pixel from three to one changed nothing (180ms ->
1007:  * 194ms, inside the noise), which is what ruled out access *count* and
1008:  * pointed at per-access *latency*.
1009:  *
1010:  * A bulk memcpy, by contrast, is sequential and lets the PSRAM controller
1011:  * burst.  So each needed row is copied once and then read repeatedly out of
1012:  * SRAM.
1013:  *
1014:  * Only the cropped span is staged: the centre 480 of 640 columns is quad
1015:  * indices CROP_X/2 .. (CROP_X+CROP_SIZE)/2, i.e. 240 quads = 960 bytes,
1016:  * instead of the full 1280-byte row.  Static rather than on the stack
1017:  * because this app's STACKSIZE is 4096.
1018:  */

1020: #define ROW_QUADS   (CROP_SIZE / 2)            /* 240 */
1021: #define ROW_BYTES   (ROW_QUADS * 4)            /* 960 */
1022: #define ROW_Q0      (CROP_X / 2)               /* first quad index staged */
1023: 
1024: static uint32_t g_rowbuf[ROW_QUADS];

1031:  *

1033:  *   collapsing three per-pixel PSRAM byte reads into one 32-bit read changed

1035:  *   with memcpy made it 456ms (worse).  Both were reasoning from a guess
1036:  *   about where the time went.  The numbers below separate the candidates so
1037:  *   the next change can be aimed rather than tried.
1038:  *
1039:  *   What each line isolates:
1040:  *     arith      the arithmetic alone, no frame memory touched at all
1041:  *     sram rnd   same access pattern as the real loop, but out of SRAM
1042:  *     psram seq  consecutive 32-bit reads from the capture buffer
1043:  *     psram rnd  the real loop's stride (one quad per 1.5 quads)
1044:  *     memcpy     bulk sequential PSRAM -> SRAM, the failed optimisation
1045:  *

1047:  *   cost is per-access PSRAM latency, and the fix has to reduce accesses or
1048:  *   make them cacheable -- not reorder them.
1049:  *
1050:  ****************************************************************************/

1052: #define BENCH_N  25600      /* one frame's worth of output pixels */

1054: static void preview_bench(FAR struct preview_s *p)
1055: {
1056:   FAR const volatile uint32_t *ps;
1057:   uint32_t t;
1058:   uint32_t acc = 0;
1059:   int i;
1060: 
1061:   if (p->camfd < 0 || p->bufs[0] == NULL)
1062:     {

1064:       return;
1065:     }
1066: 
1067:   ps = (FAR const volatile uint32_t *)p->bufs[0];
1068: 
1069:   t = now_ms();
1070:   for (i = 0; i < BENCH_N; i++)
1071:     {
1072:       acc += (uint32_t)(i * 409 + 128) >> 8;
1073:     }
1074: 
1075:   printf("bench: arith     %u iters in %ums\n", BENCH_N,
1076:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t));
1077: 
1078:   t = now_ms();
1079:   for (i = 0; i < BENCH_N; i++)
1080:     {
1081:       acc += g_rowbuf[i % ROW_QUADS];
1082:     }
1083: 
1084:   printf("bench: sram rnd  %u reads in %ums\n", BENCH_N,
1085:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t));
1086: 
1087:   t = now_ms();
1088:   for (i = 0; i < BENCH_N; i++)
1089:     {
1090:       acc += ps[i];
1091:     }
1092: 
1093:   printf("bench: psram seq %u reads in %ums\n", BENCH_N,
1094:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t));
1095: 
1096:   t = now_ms();
1097:   for (i = 0; i < BENCH_N; i++)
1098:     {
1099:       /* Same stride the converter uses: 3 source pixels per output pixel,
1100:        * two source pixels per quad.
1101:        */
1102: 
1103:       acc += ps[(i * 3) >> 1];
1104:     }
1105: 
1106:   printf("bench: psram rnd %u reads in %ums\n", BENCH_N,
1107:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t));
1108: 
1109:   t = now_ms();
1110:   for (i = 0; i < 160; i++)
1111:     {
1112:       memcpy(g_rowbuf, (FAR const void *)(p->bufs[0] + i * CAM_WIDTH * 2),
1113:              ROW_BYTES);
1114:     }
1115: 
1116:   printf("bench: memcpy    160 x %u bytes in %ums\n", ROW_BYTES,
1117:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t));

1119:   /* The converter's exact address sequence: 160 sampled rows, each 3 source
1120:    * rows apart, 160 quads per row.  The plain "psram rnd" case above stays
1121:    * inside the first 153600 bytes, while this one walks all 614400 -- if
1122:    * PSRAM has row/page miss penalties, only this case will show them, and
1123:    * that is the difference that the flat 14ms of read+arith+write fails to
1124:    * explain against a measured 194ms convert.
1125:    */

1127:   t = now_ms();
1128:   for (i = 0; i < 160; i++)
1129:     {
1130:       FAR const volatile uint32_t *row =
1131:         (FAR const volatile uint32_t *)(p->bufs[0] +
1132:                                         (size_t)(i * 3) * CAM_WIDTH * 2);

1136:         {

1139:     }

1141:   printf("bench: psram rows 160x160 strided reads in %ums\n",

1145:    * factor.
1146:    */

1158: /****************************************************************************
1159:  * Name: preview_stats
1160:  *
1161:  * Description:
1162:  *   Objective statistics of one captured frame.
1163:  *
1164:  *   Why this exists: judging the *panel* needs a human eye or a colorimeter,
1165:  *   but judging the *source* does not.  Colour flows camera -> YUV -> RGB ->
1166:  *   panel, and everything except the last hop is measurable from software.
1167:  *   Earlier rounds asked for photographs to diagnose things that were
1168:  *   actually decidable here.
1169:  *
1170:  *   How to read the output:
1171:  *

1173:  *                 A consistent offset is the camera's white balance, and the

1175:  *                 V > 128 means the source leans red, U > 128 leans blue.
1176:  *     Y min/max   The usable dynamic range.  A washed-out ("greyish")
1177:  *                 picture with correct decoding usually means Y occupies far

1181:  *                 flat, low-contrast frame.

1184:  *   measured 0.23us each) while still covering the whole frame.

1198:   uint32_t vabs = 0;
1199:   uint32_t csat = 0;      /* samples with |U-128|>16 or |V-128|>16 */

1201:   int ymax = 0;
1202:   int umin = 255;
1203:   int umax = 0;
1204:   int vmin = 255;
1205:   int vmax = 0;
1206:   uint32_t n = 0;
1207:   uint32_t i;
1208: 
1209:   memset(hist, 0, sizeof(hist));
1210: 
1211:   for (i = 0; i < nquads; i += 4)
1212:     {
1213:       uint32_t quad = q[i];
1214: 
1215:       /* Same byte offsets the decoder uses (default V Y1 U Y0), so the
1216:        * numbers below label the same channels the picture is built from.
1217:        */
1218: 
1219:       int u  = (int)((quad >> (ord->off_u * 8)) & 0xff);
1220:       int y0 = (int)((quad >> (ord->off_y0 * 8)) & 0xff);
1221:       int v  = (int)((quad >> (ord->off_v * 8)) & 0xff);
1222:       int y1 = (int)((quad >> (ord->off_y1 * 8)) & 0xff);
1223:       int ya = (y0 + y1) / 2;
1224: 
1225:       usum += (uint32_t)u;
1226:       vsum += (uint32_t)v;
1227:       ysum += (uint32_t)ya;
1228: 
1229:       uabs += (uint32_t)(u > 128 ? u - 128 : 128 - u);
1230:       vabs += (uint32_t)(v > 128 ? v - 128 : 128 - v);
1231: 
1232:       if ((u > 144 || u < 112) || (v > 144 || v < 112))
1233:         {
1234:           csat++;
1235:         }
1236: 
1237:       if (u < umin)
1238:         {
1239:           umin = u;
1240:         }
1241: 
1242:       if (u > umax)
1243:         {
1244:           umax = u;
1245:         }
1246: 
1247:       if (v < vmin)
1248:         {
1249:           vmin = v;
1250:         }
1251: 
1252:       if (v > vmax)
1253:         {
1254:           vmax = v;
1255:         }
1256: 
1257:       if (ya < ymin)
1258:         {
1259:           ymin = ya;
1260:         }
1261: 
1262:       if (ya > ymax)
1263:         {
1264:           ymax = ya;
1265:         }

1267:       hist[ya >> 4]++;

1270: 
1271:   if (n == 0)

1273:       printf("stats: no samples\n");
1274:       return;
1275:     }
1276: 
1277:   printf("stats: samples=%u  Y mean=%u min=%d max=%d span=%d\n",
1278:          (unsigned int)n, (unsigned int)(ysum / n), ymin, ymax,
1279:          ymax - ymin);

1281:          "V mean=%u (dev %+d) range=%d..%d\n",
1282:          (unsigned int)(usum / n), (int)(usum / n) - 128, umin, umax,
1283:          (unsigned int)(vsum / n), (int)(vsum / n) - 128, vmin, vmax);

1285:   /* Saturation, measured rather than assumed.  mean|U-128| / mean|V-128| is
1286:    * how far the chroma actually swings from neutral; a colourful scene gives

1293:          (unsigned int)(uabs / n), (unsigned int)(vabs / n),
